social.title: Live Jazz at Smalls Jazz Club
social.description: Smalls runs sessions until 4am in a below-street-level West Village room that holds 60 people max — $25 cover, no dress code, and musicians who could be anywhere and chose to be here.
social.bonus: Stay for the late session after midnight — the room changes completely when the tourists clear out.

social.title: Private Karaoke Room in Koreatown
social.description: Book a private room on 32nd Street in K-Town at Gagopa or Chorus — booths fit 4 to 12, they pour their own cocktails, and the per-hour rental runs all night with no judgment and proper sound systems that reward commitment.
social.bonus: Everyone performs one song they've never sung before. No safe choices. No passing.

social.title: Late Set at The Comedy Cellar
social.description: The West Village basement where stand-up was sharpened by generations — the 11pm weekend set is when surprise drop-ins happen and the crowd is loose enough for the room to go anywhere.
social.bonus: Buy a round for the table next to you after. Start a conversation before the next set begins.

social.title: Rooftop Bar Crawl Through Williamsburg
social.description: Three rooftops in one evening: start at Westlight at the William Vale for the skyline shot, move to the Ides at the Wythe Hotel for the crowd, and finish at 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge for the harbor view — each stop earns the next.
social.bonus: Walk between bars — no Ubers until the crawl is complete.

foodie.title: Late-Night Tonkotsu at Ippudo Westside
foodie.description: Ippudo's West Village location fills every night until midnight with Hakata-style tonkotsu broth that's been simmered for 18 hours — the pork buns arrive first, the broth hits last, and the energy of the room keeps the whole thing moving.
foodie.bonus: Order the Akamaru Modern and the pork buns. Nothing else. No substitutions.

foodie.title: Dim Sum Morning in Flushing, Queens
foodie.description: Downtown Flushing's covered markets and 7-train strip deliver the most alive food scene in NYC before 10am — har gow, soup dumplings, scallion pancakes, and turnip cakes from a dozen counters within two blocks.
foodie.bonus: Point to one thing on a cart or counter you can't identify. Order it. Eat before looking it up.

foodie.title: The Square Slice at Di Fara Pizza
foodie.description: Dom DeMarco's Midwood institution has been hand-stretching and scissor-cutting fresh basil over the same margherita since 1964 — arrive before noon, join the line, and watch the ritual at the counter before the first bite justifies every minute of the trip.
foodie.bonus: Order one regular and one square slice. Decide which is better and be ready to defend it.

foodie.title: Oysters at Grand Central Oyster Bar
foodie.description: Hidden below Grand Central Terminal's concourse since 1913, this tile-vaulted dining room rotates 30+ oyster varieties with cold Muscadet alongside stews, pan roasts, and a crowd that genuinely doesn't care about being seen.
foodie.bonus: Ask the shucker which oyster is best today. Take their recommendation without looking it up first.

chill.title: Browse the Stacks at The Strand Bookstore
chill.description: 18 miles of books across four floors at the corner of 12th and Broadway — rare editions in the basement, review galleys in the bins out front, and a staircase that makes you forget you had a plan for the afternoon.
chill.bonus: Buy one book you'd never normally pick — judge it by the first paragraph only. If the first sentence grabs you, it's yours.

chill.title: High Line Walk at Golden Hour
chill.description: The 1.45-mile elevated park cuts through Chelsea and Hell's Kitchen with Hudson River views at every gap — hit it at 6pm in summer when the light drops behind New Jersey, the crowd thins, and the city slows down for an hour.
chill.bonus: Walk the entire thing without your phone out. Look at the city instead of through a lens.

chill.title: Rooftop Drinks at 230 Fifth
chill.description: The biggest outdoor rooftop bar in NYC sits atop a 20-story Flatiron building with 360-degree skyline views and heated igloos in winter — bigger and less pretentious than the hotel bars, which is exactly why it delivers.
chill.bonus: Arrive before dark. Watch the skyline lights come on. Don't leave until the last building is lit.

chill.title: Slow Sunday at The Metropolitan Museum
chill.description: Pick one wing — Greek and Roman, arms and armor, or the 19th-century European galleries — and go slowly instead of trying to cover everything; the Met is overwhelming at speed and extraordinary at leisure.
chill.bonus: Find one piece you'd want in your home. Sit in front of it for ten full minutes without moving on.

active.title: Clay Courts at Central Park Tennis Center
active.description: The 26 red clay courts at Central Park Tennis Center sit just above the Reservoir with the skyline framing the tree line beyond the baseline — book online the night before, rent rackets on-site, and you're playing within 20 minutes of the subway.
active.bonus: Play to 6 games straight. Winner buys coffee from the café on the way out.

active.title: Skate the Bryant Park Rink
active.description: The free rink behind the New York Public Library opens each October through February with the Midtown skyline as a backdrop — admission is free, skate rental is cheap, and the crowd is genuinely mixed in a way that hotel ice rinks never are.
active.bonus: Complete one full lap without touching the wall. Then do two more.

active.title: Stand-Up Paddle on the Hudson River
active.description: Manhattan Kayak rents SUP boards from Pier 84 on the Hudson — catch the glassy water early Saturday morning and paddle south toward the Statue of Liberty with the city on one side and the Palisades on the other.
active.bonus: Paddle far enough south that the Statue of Liberty stands alone with no other structure framing it. Then turn back.

active.title: Run Brooklyn Bridge to DUMBO and Back
active.description: Cross the Brooklyn Bridge pedestrian path into DUMBO, run the waterfront loop past the carousel, cross back on the Manhattan Bridge walkway, and you've done a 4-mile circuit with uninterrupted views of the entire downtown skyline.
active.bonus: Go before 7am — the bridge is clear, the light is low, and the span is yours.

adventure.title: Axe Throwing at Kick Axe Brooklyn
adventure.description: A converted Gowanus warehouse with 15 throwing lanes, craft beer on tap, and a competitive scoring format that turns a casual Tuesday into a grudge match — the staff teach you in ten minutes and you'll be hooked in twenty.
adventure.bonus: Play sudden-death round — one throw each, closest to bullseye wins. Loser picks up the first round.

adventure.title: Free Kayak at Pier 26 Downtown Boathouse
adventure.description: Downtown Boathouse runs free 20-minute kayak loans every weekend morning in summer from Pier 26 — paddle into the Hudson with Lower Manhattan behind you and the Jersey Palisades ahead, no reservation needed.
adventure.bonus: Paddle to the midpoint and sit still in the current for 60 seconds without talking.

adventure.title: Rock Climb at The Cliffs LIC
adventure.description: NYC's largest climbing gym spans 30,000 sq ft of textured walls and roofs across a converted Queens warehouse — show up to the bouldering cave on a weeknight and you'll leave with beta from strangers who climb two grades above you.
adventure.bonus: Finish a V4 or higher before leaving — pick one that intimidates you and don't come down until it's done.
